Flashmorph/multimorph.description: Upon reaching 5th level, a warshaper receives one of two abilities depending on how she changes form. If the warshaper possesses an at-will form-changing capability - such as the change shape ability, the shapechanger subtype, or an at-will polymorph spell-like ability - she gains flashmorph, which lets her shift form as a move action. If instead she uses the polymorph spell, has polymorph as a spell-like ability with limited daily uses, or possesses wild shape, she gains multimorph. Multimorph permits the warshaper to assume different forms multiple times within a single use of whatever spell, spell-like ability, or class feature grants her shapeshifting. For instance, a wizard/warshaper could spend 2 minutes as a troll, then switch to a red dragon for 4 minutes, and use the remaining duration as a hill giant. Each subsequent transformation requires a standard action, and only the initial change restores hit points. If the warshaper reverts to her natural form, the spell, spell-like ability, or wild shape usage ends immediately.

Morphic Body.description: Starting at 2nd level, a warshaper exercises fine-tuned command over her physical structure to enhance her power and endurance. She receives a +4 bonus to Strength and a +4 bonus to Constitution.

Morphic Healing.description: At 4th level, a warshaper learns to reshape her flesh around injuries, smoothing damaged tissue back into wholeness. She gains fast healing 2. Additionally, by spending a full-round action and succeeding on a Concentration check (DC equal to her total damage sustained), she can restore 10 hit points.

Morphic Immunities.description: A warshaper becomes skilled at relocating and redistributing vital organs throughout her body to protect them from targeted strikes. She is immune to stunning and critical hits.

Morphic Reach.description: At 3rd level or higher, a warshaper can abruptly extend her limbs, neck, or other body parts, increasing her reach by 5 feet beyond that of the creature whose form she has taken. Other creatures cannot tell the warshaper has extended reach until she actually uses it.

Morphic Weapons.description: By spending a move action, a warshaper can sprout natural weapons like claws or fangs, gaining a natural attack that deals damage appropriate for her current form's size. These grown weapons do not need to be ones the assumed creature naturally has. For instance, a warshaper in the form of an ettin (Large giant) could produce claws dealing 1d6 damage, or horns for a gore attack dealing 1d8 damage. If the warshaper's current shape already includes a natural weapon of that type, the weapon inflicts damage as though the creature were one size category larger. As an example, a warshaper who used wild shape to become a dire wolf (Large animal) could enlarge her jaws, making her bite deal 2d6 damage (as for a Huge animal) rather than the standard 1d8. The warshaper may alter her morphic weapons as frequently as she wishes, even when using a shapeshifting method like polymorph or wild shape that normally prevents further changes after the first transformation.

Weapon and Armor Proficiency.description: This prestige class does not grant proficiency with any weapons or armor.

These morphic weapons need not be natural weapons that the creature already possesses. For example, a warshaper polymorphed into an ettin (Large giant) could grow a claw that deals 1d6 points of damage, or horns for a gore attack that deals 1d8 points of damage. classFeatures.description: A 5th-level warshaper gains one of two class features. If the warshaper has the ability to change form at will, such as from the change shape ability, the shapechanger subtype, or a polymorph spell-like ability, it gains the flashmorph class feature, allowing it to change form as a move action. If it casts the polymorph spell, has polymorph as a spell-like ability usable less often than at will, or has the wild shape class feature, it instead gains the multimorph class feature. Multimorph allows a warshaper to change forms multiple times during the duration of the spell, spell-like ability, or class feature that enables her to change form. For example, a wizard/warshaper could polymorph into a troll for 2 minutes, then change into a red dragon for 4 minutes, and then spend the rest of the spell's duration in the form of a hill giant. Each change requires a standard action, and only the first transformation heals the warshaper. If the warshaper changes into its natural form, the spell, spell-like ability, or use of wild shape ends.
